name: Lost In Translation
summary: Party bluffing game where players invent fake translations of signs, movie titles and idioms to fool each other.
rules_text: Each round one player is the Editor. The Editor draws a card of three types: Picture with covered words, foreign movie title, or foreign idiom with literal translation, and reads the prompt aloud without revealing the true translation. All other players write a funny or plausible fake translation on their sheet; the Editor copies the true answer onto theirs. Sheets are collected, Editor reads all answers including the real one with equal tone. If any fake exactly matches the real, that player scores 3 and sits out voting. Otherwise, clockwise from Editor's left, each player votes for which answer they think is real; you may vote for your own but scores nothing. Scoring: 1 point per vote your fake receives, 2 points for voting correctly, Editor gets 2 if no one finds the truth, plus 1 for Editor's favorite fake. After 10 rounds highest total wins.
rating_reason: Balderdash-style translation bluffing, voting, hidden info excellent fit.
